alex_support: FYI customer reported intermittent 500s and very high p99 (3.2s) on /v1/generate yesterday ~09:30 UTC. They can reproduce occasionally. Asked for quick repro scripts + request ids so we can triage.

mike_oncall: Can you paste the request-id they saw in the response headers? that speeds things up. Also which SDK (py/js/go)?

alex_support: customer says header x-request-id: rq_6b7f2c9a. Using our Node SDK in prod but they were able to curl it too. Attaching their minimal curl they used (sanitized):

alex_support: ```curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-ggml-13b","input":"hello world"}' --max-time 10```

ingrid_engineer: thanks. please ask for the full response headers (raw) and the exact body when it 500s. Also ask them to run with `-v` to capture TLS handshake stuff. Could be intermittent routing failure or backend OOM.

nate_sre: quick repro scripts so we can reproduce here. Provide minimal py/js/go that include header logging and a short retry loop. I'll paste trimmed examples:

nate_sre: Python (requests):

nate_sre: ```python
import requests
import time

url = "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"
headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer $TOKEN", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
payload = {"model": "rwd-ggml-13b", "input": "test repro"}

for i in range(3):
    r = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers, timeout=8)
    print(i, r.status_code, r.headers.get('x-request-id'))
    print(r.text[:400])
    if r.status_code == 200:
        break
    time.sleep(1)
```

nate_sre: Node (fetch):

nate_sre: ```js
const fetch = require('node-fetch')
const url = 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate'
const body = JSON.stringify({model:'rwd-ggml-13b', input:'test repro'})

async function run(){
  for(let i=0;i<3;i++){
    const res = await fetch(url, {method:'POST', body, headers:{'Authorization':`Bearer ${process.env.TOKEN}`,'Content-Type':'application/json'}, timeout:8000})
    console.log(i, res.status, res.headers.get('x-request-id'))
    const txt = await res.text()
    console.log(txt.slice(0,400))
    if(res.status===200) break
    await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,1000))
  }
}
run()
```

nate_sre: Go (net/http):

nate_sre: ```go
package main
import (
  "bytes"
  "fmt"
  "io/ioutil"
  "net/http"
  "os"
  "time"
)
func main(){
  url := "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"
  payload := []byte(`{"model":"rwd-ggml-13b","input":"test repro"}`)
  client := &http.Client{Timeout: 8 * time.Second}
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", url, bytes.NewBuffer(payload))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+os.Getenv("TOKEN"))
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  for i:=0;i<3;i++{
    resp, err := client.Do(req)
    if err!=nil{fmt.Println(i, "err:", err); time.Sleep(time.Second); continue}
    id := resp.Header.Get("x-request-id")
    body, _ := ioutil.ReadAll(resp.Body)
    fmt.Println(i, resp.StatusCode, id)
    fmt.Println(string(body)[:400])
    resp.Body.Close()
    if resp.StatusCode==200 {break}
    time.Sleep(time.Second)
  }
}
```

ingrid_engineer: also request they capture the debug bundle from their side: full curl `-v` output, the exact request body (including any special chars), and the response headers + body when it 500s. Ask them to include the SDK version + Node/npm/yarn output if using JS.

alex_support: forwarded the scripts and asked for: raw headers, the full response body when it fails, and a contiguous timeline (local time + UTC) for each occurrence. Customer replied with one more header set: `x-request-id: rq_6b7f2c9a`, `server: rwd-gw-12`, `x-upstream-instance: rwd-serve-47`, response body `{"error":"internal server error","code":"INTERNAL"}`. Attaching sanitized log excerpt:

alex_support: ```[2026-03-01T09:30:12Z] request_id=rq_6b7f2c9a route=/v1/generate lat_ms=3210 upstream=rwd-serve-47 status=500 error="oom while decoding kv"
[2026-03-01T09:30:12Z] request_id=rq_6b7f2c9a workers=4 queue_ms=12```

mike_oncall: that log line is super helpful — "oom while decoding kv" indicates a model-serving OOM during KV-cache expansion. Could be caused by unusually long input or concurrency spike. Ask them for the input size / tokens length and whether they have any surprising prefix.

nate_sre: quick triage steps for customer to run so we can correlate traces:
1) Run the provided minimal script (py or js) with env TOKEN set and `--log-level=debug` equivalent.
2) Add header `X-Debug: 1` to force richer traces from our gateway (note: only visible to support).
3) If they can, reproduce with a pinned model variant `rwd-ggml-13b-compact` to see if quantized variant avoids OOM.
4) Send us the `x-request-id` + full curl -v output.

ingrid_engineer: I'll check server rwd-serve-47 logs for that request id, see if it hit autorestart or GC thrash. Nate, could you also check if our kernel selection logs show any excessive kv-memory reservation at 3.2s?

nate_sre: on it. tagging @devops-bot to pull the host logs for rwd-serve-47 and grep for rq_6b7f2c9a.

devops-bot: started log extraction job job-8841. ETA ~45s. results will be uploaded to /tmp/support/extracts/job-8841.tar.gz

mike_oncall: thanks everyone. alex, please tell customer: run the minimal script, include env TOKEN and `X-Debug: 1` header, capture curl -v output, and try the `-compact` model as an experiment. Also ask them to avoid sending very large context; if they must, ask for an example payload. We'll prioritize once they share the full curl -v and the new x-request-id if it reoccurs. :pray:

alex_support: will do. closing loop with customer now and will paste any new x-request-ids back here when they come in. :phone:
